title: Non-modal filter composer with live column previews for virtual tables
creator: Ana Rivera
description: Introduce a non-modal, inline filter composer that attaches to column headers and surfaces live previews of filtered results. The composer must work smoothly with the virtualized table renderer, respect density modes (compact, default, spacious), and avoid layout jank or scroll jumps when applying previews. This ticket covers design specs, behavior edge-cases, a prototype, and handoff notes for engineering.
motivation: Current filter UX uses a modal/overlay that blocks context and makes rapid exploratory filtering slow. For large virtualized datasets, users need immediate feedback on how filter expressions affect visible rows without losing table context or breaking virtualization. The new composer should support quick multi-field filter composition, visible match counts, and a safe preview mode that does not permanently mutate state until the user confirms.
proposed_design:
- Composer opens anchored to the column header as a lightweight panel (not full-screen modal).
- Live preview: composer shows a live, sample-based preview: a small rowset snapshot and a matched rows count badge.
- Preview mode is read-only: user can see previews without committing filter state; 'Apply' commits and closes composer; 'Preview' updates the snapshot only.
- Composer supports field suggestions, boolean operators, and a simple expression builder for ranges and partial matches.
- Density-aware UI: in compact mode the composer reduces padding, uses smaller controls, and collapses advanced options under a single chevron.
- Keyboard traps: composer supports Enter to apply, Escape to close, arrow navigation between tokens, and typeahead for suggestions.
- When open, composer does not change table scroll position. Preview works by querying a sampling API or running a client-side sample against already-fetched rows when available.
tradeoffs:
- Live preview accuracy vs performance: sampling gives statistical preview counts quickly, but exact counts require server-side queries which may be slow. We will surface an estimated count and a confidence indicator.
- Inline composer increases header complexity and may slightly increase DOM size; this is offset by improved discovery and faster workflow.
- For very wide tables, composer width needs adaptive behavior; we'll prioritize keeping it within the viewport and allow an overflow panel anchored to the header.
accessibility_considerations:
- Composer has role='dialog' with aria-modal='false' to indicate non-blocking behavior.
- Announce when preview results change (e.g., 'Preview: 12 rows match').
- Ensure focus management: focus returns to the column header when composer closes; keyboard users can open composer with Space/Enter on header filter button.
- Controls must have visible focus styles across density modes and pass color contrast requirements.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Composer opens from column header with a single keystroke or mouse click and is non-modal (does not block table interaction outside its area).
AC-2: Live preview shows a sampled row snapshot and an estimated match count within 2s for 95% of requests in staging. Confidence indicator displayed for sampled results.
AC-3: Applying a filter (Apply) commits state and updates table without scroll jump; Preview updates snapshot without committing state or changing table scroll position.
AC-4: Composer adapts to compact/default/spacious density tokens and respects typography/spacing tokens from the design system.
AC-5: Full keyboard support validated: open, navigate tokens, apply, cancel, and focus returns to header.
implementation_notes:
- Engineering will implement a feature flag 'inline_filter_composer_v1' for gradual rollout.
- Backend endpoints: /filters/preview that accepts a filter expression and returns estimated count + sample rows. Preview can fall back to client-side sampling when offline.
- Debounce preview queries at 300ms; allow cancelation of inflight requests.
- Virtualization integration: preview responses must include visible index hints so client can map sample rows to positions without forcing full dataset fetch.
- Provide a small prototype in Figma + interactive Storybook component demonstrating open/close, preview state, and density variations.
